scope: Independent synthetic Python Kubernetes-API state regression; no Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, native container or hosted call.
finding: Removing a terminal Pod finalizer before durable per-UID exit proof could lose its identity through immediate garbage collection and permanently block later recovery of a mixed group.
correction: Persist exact observed termination receipts in the Deployment journal before finalizer removal; retain mixed groups; recapture the remaining journal after initial restore.
test: Unchanged independent script: two captured Storage Pods A/B; A terminal and immediately garbage-collected on finalizer removal, then B terminal and fresh-run restore.
red: A removed; fresh recovery refused despite B terminal.
green: A retained while B runs; after B exits fresh recovery completes and clears pending journal.

 f.s['expected_workloads']['storage']['replicas']=2
 dep=f.cluster.resources['deployment','storage'];dep['spec']['replicas']=2;dep['status'].update(readyReplicas=2,updatedReplicas=2)
 a=f.cluster.resources['pod','storage-pod'];b=copy.deepcopy(a);b['metadata'].update(name='storage-pod-b',uid=str(uuid.uuid4()));f.cluster.resources['pod','storage-pod-b']=b
 captured=f.a.capture(f.s);f.a.protect_pods(captured,f.a.nonce);f.a.stop(captured,f.a.nonce)
 a['metadata']['deletionTimestamp']='2026-11-04T00:00:00Z'

 print(json.dumps(result))
